Unlike dense voxel grids which scale poorly with resolution, HashGrid uses spatial hashing to map voxel coordinates to a compact embedding table, reducing computational operations by approximately 70% compared to direct large implicit network queries [S2, unofficial].
- **Feature Initialization**: Performed using a multi-resolution Hash Grid with 16 levels, spanning a resolution range from $N_{min} = 16$ to $N_{max} = 8192$ with a geometric growth factor.
- **Implicit Geometry Decoder**: A shallow MLP with 2 hidden layers of 64 units and ReLU activations.
- **RGB Network**: Shares an identical architecture with the geometry decoder (2 layers, 64 hidden units).
Hash Grid Neural Fields originated from the need to accelerate neural rendering on consumer hardware.

The core mechanism of multi-resolution hash encoding was popularized by [InstantNGP](https://nvlabs.github.io/instant-ngp/), which demonstrated that sparse hash tables could overcome the memory and computational bottlenecks of dense voxel grids and standard MLPs [S2, S3, unofficial].
